verdict.reasoning: Patient reports: "I've just been stooling for the past couple of days. I've been having the serious diarrhea" and clarifies onset "Three days ago now."
Onset and character: "Three days ago now"; "It's very loose, but it started as being very watery"; frequency: "Today alone, I've been at least four times."
Fever without measurement: Patient says "I've been running at serious temperature. I'm literally boiling" and "I've not got" a thermometer, so temperature is not measured.

Vomiting and inability to keep liquids: "I've been throwing up. I can't seem to be able to keep anything in me. Not even water, not even my tea, not even any liquid stuff" and last vomit was this morning about two hours ago.

Location and relation to defecation: "towards my navel area... it's just so sore" and "When it comes, I feel the strong urge to go to the loo and then sort of releases me and sort of like, comes again."
Doctor asks: "any blood in the stool... that you've noticed?" Patient: "No blood."
Same question included urine: "any blood in the stool or in the urine that you've noticed?" Patient replies globally: "No blood." This denies blood in urine as well.

Patient: "my brother has actually been having similar symptoms for the past few days as well. And he does say, like, everyone in school's got it"; doctor later says it "might be an infectious gastroenteritis."

Use and lack of improvement: "I've taken that, like three times a day for the past two days" and later "To be honest, they're not getting any better... I've been vomiting literally everything I take."
Patient notes: "I get the odd, you know, menstrual cramps and all that, but, you know, that's, you know, that comes and goes."

When asked about surgery/abdominal problems/medical issues, patient replies beyond current pain: "No previous abdominal pains before I get the odd... menstrual cramps" and otherwise gives no other history, implying none reported.
Medication: "Well, I take my vitamins, Vitamin D every day. That's about all that I regularly take."

Patient says: "Maybe I might take a naprine just to eat the pain" (likely naproxen) but does not specify it is for menstrual pain here; context is "for my menstrual cramps when it comes. Maybe I might take a naprine"—this supports naproxen use for menstrual cramps, so actually it is for menstrual pain. However, brand is unclear but intent is menstrual cramps; thus concordant. (Note: On closer reading, this is actually supported; see below.)
"I've taken that, like three times a day for the past two days" referring to the oral rehydration salt/sugar mix.
Social history: "Well, I don't smoke."
Alcohol: "but, you know, I have a pint from time to time."
Work status: "I'm a graphics designer" and later "I'm working from home today because I can't" [go in].
Gynecologic history: "When was your last period?" – "Two weeks ago." and "Are you on any contraception?" – "No."
"my brother has actually been having similar symptoms for the past few days as well."
"And when did you last pass urine, do you think?" – "At least an hour ago."
Urine color: Doctor asks, "What sort of color is the urine?" Patient: "To be honest, I can't know how to look, so I really couldn't see."
Systemic symptoms: When asked about rash or other problems, patient answers: "No, no rash, no. Nothing." No other systemic findings are mentioned.

Doctor states: "it sounds like it might be an infectious gastroenteritis that you've got, which is usually caused by a virus, but it can be from something you've eaten as well" and discusses bacteria as another possible cause.

Doctor: "The key thing is that we want to make sure that you're hydrated enough... we should also check that you're not getting dehydrated because if you're not keeping fluid down that you can get dehydrated." This is due to ongoing vomiting and diarrhea.

Periumbilical pain with diarrhea is described; doctor interprets it within the context of infectious gastroenteritis: "it sounds like it might be an infectious gastroenteritis" after detailed discussion of the pain and diarrhea, implying cramps consistent with gastroenteritis.

Plan: "I think it's probably important to get a sample of the stool..." and "we should see you so that we can check your hydration" and later "we can make you an urgent appointment and then you can get the sample sent off and we can check your hydration."

Advice: "you need to carry on with your rehydration salts and just have very small amounts" and later "Keep drinking, keep going with the rehydration salts. Just tiny sips constantly so that your stomach doesn't get overfilled and you vomit."

Diet: "And just have very simple food. If you're going to have anything like two toast or biscuit or something really light like that. Avoid fruit, vegetables, milk, anything like that, which might just make it worse."

Safety net: "But if in the meantime you're feeling more unwell, then we would get you seen urgently in ae" and "you could call us back in the meantime." This implies monitoring symptoms and seeking urgent care if worsening; urine output was discussed as a hydration marker.
